entries.title: OFAC designates four individuals and eleven entities tied to Cartel del Noreste, including the La Molienda racetrack and a quarter-horse stable
entries.facts: On October 13, 2026 the U.S. Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control designated four individuals and eleven entities under Executive Order 14059 and Executive Order 13224, as amended by Executive Order 13886, in an action Treasury titled "Treasury Targets Cartel del Noreste's Horse Racing Enterprise and Expansive Criminal Network." The designated entities include Club La Molienda, also known as La Molienda Race Track and Restaurant Bar La Molienda, of Nuevo Laredo, Tamaulipas, listed for sports facility operation, and Cuadra San Dibanh of Anahuac, Nuevo Leon, listed for horse raising, together with construction, fuel-wholesale and transport companies. Treasury's release states that "CDN has a long history of money laundering through the American Quarter Horse racing industry," that La Molienda "is a horse racetrack, restaurant, and bar located on the outskirts of Nuevo Laredo," that "As the most prominent racetrack in Nuevo Laredo, La Molienda generates revenue for CDN," that "La Molienda and Casino Centenario entered a strategic gambling partnership" with "Casino Centenario, a casino just miles from the U.S. border," and that one designated individual is "involved in horse racing in both Mexico and the United States." The OFAC recent-actions listing for the designations records no digital currency addresses for any designated person or entity. Treasury states the action was taken in coordination with Mexico's financial intelligence unit, the UIF.
entries.source_label: OFAC recent actions, Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Designations (Oct. 13, 2026), with quoted language from Treasury press release sb0656
entries.relevant_to: racetracks and racebooks, casinos, gaming operators, sanctions screening and AML compliance functions
